173:   async setAvatar(data: Uint8Array | null): Promise<void> {
174:     if (data) {
175:       if (data.byteLength > 100 * 1024) {
176:         throw new Error("Avatar too large (max 100 KB)");
177:       }
178:       // Verify the data starts with a known image magic-byte header.
179:       let isJpeg = data[0] === 0xFF && data[1] === 0xD8 && data[2] === 0xFF;
180:       let isPng = data[0] === 0x89 && data[1] === 0x50 && data[2] === 0x4E && data[3] === 0x47;
181:       if (!isJpeg && !isPng) {
182:         throw new Error("Avatar must be a JPEG or PNG image");
183:       }
184:     }
185:     // Avatar data lives in KV (global), not the user's DO storage, so we
186:     // read/write it directly here to avoid routing through the DO location.
187:     let userId = this.#userId.name!;
188:     if (data) {
189:       await this.env.AVATARS.put(userId, data);
190:     } else {
191:       await this.env.AVATARS.delete(userId);
192:     }
193:   }

216:   async #openGadgetInternal(id: string, shareKey?: string,
217:                             configureObservers?: RpcStub<ObserverConfigCallback>)
218:       : Promise<NativeRpcStub<Overseer>> {
219:     let userId = this.#userId.toString();
220:     let profileId = this.#userId.name!;
221:     let overseerId;
222:     try {
223:       overseerId = this.overseers.idFromString(id);
224:     } catch {
225:       throw createOpenGadgetError(OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceNotFound);
226:     }
227:     let overseer = this.overseers.get(overseerId);
228: 
229:     // HACK: Detect loss of the connection to the DO by:
230:     // - Pass a callback to overseer.open() which it should call when the session is disposed.
231:     // - Detect if the callback itself is disposed before being called, suggesting the connection
232:     //   was lost.
233:     // If the connection is lost, we abort this I/O context, which kills the WebSocket from the
234:     // client, forcing it to engage its reconnect logic, which should recover.
235:     // TODO: Implement onRpcBroken() in the built-in RPC system, matching Cap'n Web, and use that
236:     //   instead.
237:     // TODO: Consider how to reconnect to one DO without resetting the whole WebSocket. Probably
238:     //   needs new code on the client side. However, typically a client only ever opens one
239:     //   gadget at a time (since each tab is a separate client), so it's probably fine for now.
240:     let closed = false;
241:     let started = false;
242:     let notifyClosed = () => {
243:       closed = true;
244:     };
245:     (notifyClosed as any)[Symbol.dispose] = () => {
246:       if (started && !closed) {
247:         // this.ctx.abort() would be nicer here, but it is still marked experimental in the
248:         // workers runtime.
249:         this.abortSession(new Error(`lost connection to workspace DO (gadget ${id})`));
250:       }
251:     }
252: 
253:     let result;
254:     try {
255:       result = await overseer.open(userId, profileId, notifyClosed, shareKey, configureObservers);
256:     } catch (err) {
257:       // A denial proves this user's listing for the workspace is stale: revocation tries to drop it
258:       // (refreshAffectedCollaboratorListings), but that push is best-effort. Only catches entries
259:       // they click; others stay frozen at revocation, as a disconnected collaborator gets no pushes.
260:       if (getOpenGadgetErrorCode(err) === OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES.workspaceAccessDenied) {
261:         await this.#user.forgetSharedGadget(id);
262:       }
263:       throw err;
264:     }
265:     started = true;
266:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
267:       event_name: "gadget_opened",
268:       user_id: userId,
269:       gadget_id: id,
270:       source: shareKey ? "share_key" : "direct",
271:     });
272:     return result;
273:   }

433:   async newGadgetFromBlueprint(
434:     blueprintId: string,
435:     bindings: Record<string, BlueprintBindingAssignment>
436:   ): Promise<RpcStub<Overseer>> {
437:     // 1. Read blueprint from KV.
438:     let kvRecord = await readBlueprintKvRecord(this.env, blueprintId);
439:     if (!kvRecord) throw new Error("Blueprint not found.");
440: 
441:     // 2. Read gzip-compressed Yjs doc from R2 and decompress.
442:     let codeBytes = await readBlueprintContent(this.env, blueprintId, kvRecord.metadata.version);
443:     if (!codeBytes) throw new Error("Blueprint content not found in R2.");
444: 
445:     // 3. Create new Overseer DO (same as newGadget()).
446:     let id = this.overseers.newUniqueId().toString();
447:     await this.#user.newGadget(id, kvRecord.metadata.title);
448:     let overseerResult = await this.#openGadgetInternal(id);
449: 
450:     // 4. Initialize from blueprint code.
451:     let overseerDo = this.overseers.get(this.overseers.idFromString(id));
452:     await overseerDo.initializeFromBlueprint(codeBytes, kvRecord.metadata.title,
453:         deploymentOutputForBlueprint(await readAdminConfig(this.env), blueprintId,
454:             sanitizeBlueprintOutput(kvRecord.metadata.output)));
455: 
456:     // 5. Create gatekeepers from assignments and bind them into the workspace's (only) gadget.
457:     let metadata = await overseerResult.getMetadata();
458:     using gadget = await overseerResult.getGadget(metadata.defaultGadgetId!);
459: 
460:     // Defensively put blueprint bindings into a map (not a raw object) until we've had a chance to
461:     // validate the names.
462:     let blueprintBindings = new Map(Object.entries(kvRecord.metadata.bindings));
463:     let gadgetId = metadata.defaultGadgetId!;
464: 
465:     // Create gatekeepers in two phases: first every non-spawner binding (binding the
466:     // non-spawnerOnly ones into the gadget, and recording each created gatekeeper's id by
467:     // binding name), then the agent spawners, whose configs reference the phase-one results
468:     // symbolically (see SpawnerEnvTarget).
469:     let createdIds = new Map<string, WorkpieceId>();
470:     let gkPromises: Promise<void>[] = [];
471: 
472:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
473:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
474:       if (!blueprintBinding) {
475:         throw new Error(`Unknown binding name: ${bindingName}`);
476:       }
477: 
478:       gkPromises.push((async () => {
479:         let gk;
480:         if (assignment.type === "gatekeeper") {
481:           gk = await overseerResult.newGatekeeper(assignment.accountId, assignment.resourceUrl);
482:           if (!gk) {
483:             throw new Error(`Failed to create gatekeeper for binding "${bindingName}".`);
484:           }
485:         } else if (assignment.type === "aiModel") {
486:           gk = await overseerResult.newAiModelGatekeeper(assignment.modelId);
487:         } else {
488:           return;  // agent spawners are created in phase two
489:         }
490:         try {
491:           let id = await gk.getId();
492:           createdIds.set(bindingName, id);
493:           // A spawnerOnly binding exists purely to feed some spawner's env; it is not bound
494:           // into the gadget itself.
495:           if (!blueprintBinding.spawnerOnly) {
496:             await gadget.bind(bindingName, id);
497:           }
498:         } finally {
499:           gk[Symbol.dispose]();
500:         }
501:       })());
502:     }
503: 
504:     await Promise.all(gkPromises);
505: 
506:     // Phase two: agent spawners, with the full AgentSpawnerConfig reconstructed -- displayName
507:     // from the binding's title, modelId from the assignment, and env resolved against the
508:     // phase-one gatekeepers and the new gadget.
509:     for (let [bindingName, assignment] of Object.entries(bindings)) {
510:       if (assignment.type !== "agentSpawner") continue;
511:       let blueprintBinding = blueprintBindings.get(bindingName);
512:       if (blueprintBinding?.type !== "agentSpawner") {
513:         throw new Error(`Binding "${bindingName}" type mismatch.`);
514:       }
515: 
516:       let env: Record<string, WorkpieceId> = {};
517:       for (let [envName, target] of Object.entries(blueprintBinding.env)) {
518:         if (target.type === "gadget") {
519:           env[envName] = gadgetId;
520:         } else {
521:           let id = createdIds.get(target.name);
522:           if (id === undefined) {
523:             throw new Error(`Agent spawner binding "${bindingName}" references binding ` +
524:                 `"${target.name}", which was not assigned.`);
525:           }
526:           env[envName] = id;
527:         }
528:       }
529: 
530:       let config: AgentSpawnerConfig = {
531:         displayName: blueprintBinding.title,
532:         modelId: assignment.modelId,
533:         env,
534:       };
535:       using gk = await overseerResult.newAgentSpawnerGatekeeper(config);
536:       await gadget.bind(bindingName, await gk.getId());
537:     }
538: 
539:     recordAnalytics(this.ctx, this.env, {
540:       event_name: "gadget_created",
541:       user_id: this.#userId.toString(),
542:       gadget_id: id,
543:       blueprint_id: blueprintId,
544:       source: "blueprint",
545:     });
546: 
547:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC stubs are compatible but the type
548:     //     system doesn't know this.
549:     return overseerResult;
550:   }

621: // result through a capability (this stub) rather than a guessable id — no login id is ever exposed

636: class PublicApiImpl extends RpcTarget implements PublicApi {

639:   constructor(private ctx: ExecutionContext, private env: Env,
640:       private abortSession: (reason: Error) => void,
641:       private accessPayload?: JWTPayload) {

652:   async startGatekeeperLogin(vendorId: string): Promise<{ url: string; attempt: RpcStub<LoginAttempt> }> {
653:     if (!getAuthGatekeeperAllowlist(this.env).includes(vendorId)) {
654:       throw new Error(`Sign-in via "${vendorId}" is not enabled on this deployment.`);
655:     }
656:     const vendor = getAuthVendorBinding(this.env, vendorId);
657:     if (!vendor) throw new Error(`No such auth gatekeeper: ${vendorId}`);
658:     const desc = await vendor.describe();
659:     if (!desc.providesAuth) throw new Error(`"${vendorId}" does not provide authentication.`);
660: 
661:     // The PendingLogin DO is the rendezvous between this request and the (separate) OAuth-callback
662:     // invocation. The client never sees its id — we hand back an `attempt` stub instead.
663:     const pendingId = this.ctx.exports.PendingLogin.newUniqueId();
664:     const pending = this.ctx.exports.PendingLogin.get(pendingId);
665:     const callback = this.ctx.exports.LoginConnectCallbackImpl(
666:         { props: { pendingId: pendingId.toString(), vendorId } });
667:     // For most providers, sign-in needs only minimal scopes to verify the user's email (the grant is
668:     // transient); capability scopes are requested later via an explicit connectAccount. Cloudflare is
669:     // the exception: signing in with Cloudflare also links AI Gateway billing, so it requests and
670:     // persists the billing-only scope set up front.
671:     const options = vendorId === CLOUDFLARE_VENDOR_ID
672:       ? { scopes: "full" as const, resourceUrlPatterns: [] }
673:       : { scopes: "auth" as const };
674:     const { url } = await vendor.connectAccount(callback, options);
675:     // @ts-expect-error Cap'n Web RPC stubs and native RPC targets are compatible but the type
676:     //     system doesn't know this.
677:     return { url, attempt: new LoginAttemptImpl(pending) };
678:   }

691:       source: "session_token",

696:   async authenticateFromCfAccess(): Promise<AuthenticatedApi> {
697:     if (!this.accessPayload) {
698:       throw createAuthError(AUTH_ERROR_CODES.notAuthenticatedWithAccess);
699:     }

701:     let email = this.accessPayload.email as string;
702:     let userId = this.users.idFromName(email);
703:     let signupsEnabled = (await readAdminConfig(this.env)).signupsEnabled;

244: async function checkGatekeeperVendorFilter(
245:     vendor: Service<GatekeeperVendor> | Service<GatekeeperUser>,
246:     vendorId: string,
247:     filter: GatekeeperVendorFilter): Promise<boolean> {
248:   try {
249:     if (filter.resourceUrl) {
250:       let resources = await vendor.getSupportedResources();
251:       let matched = false;
252:       for (let resource of resources) {
253:         if (typeof resource.urlPattern !== "string") {
254:           // Guard against gatekeepers returning a non-string urlPattern for now.
255:           //
256:           // TODO: Consider whether this is the API we want for getSupportedResources(). Is URLPattern
257:           //   even the right thing?
258:           throw new Error("Gatekeeper returned non-string urlPattern from getSupportedResources()");
259:         }
260: 
261:         if (new URLPattern(resource.urlPattern).test(filter.resourceUrl)) {
262:           matched = true;
263:           break;
264:         }
265:       }
266:       if (!matched) return false;
267:     }
268: 
269:     return true;
270:   } catch (err) {
271:     // This function is called when iterating over several gatekeepers to filter them. If one of
272:     // them throws we don't want to block the whole list, so instead log the error and assume this
273:     // gatekeeper should be filtered.
274:     logger.warn("gatekeeper filter check failed", {
275:       event: "gatekeeper.filter.check.failed", vendorId, error: err,
276:     });
277:     return false;
278:   }
279: }

304:   async authenticate(token: string): Promise<void> {
305:     let tokenBytes: Uint8Array;
306:     try {
307:       tokenBytes = Uint8Array.fromBase64(token);
308:     } catch {
309:       // A corrupt (non-Base64) token must classify as an auth failure like any other bad token,
310:       // not surface as the decoder's SyntaxError.
311:       throw createAuthError(AUTH_ERROR_CODES.invalidSessionToken);
312:     }
313:     let hash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', tokenBytes);
314:     let tokenId = new Uint8Array(hash).toHex();
315:     let session = this.storage.sessions.get(tokenId);
316:     if (!session) {
317:       throw createAuthError(AUTH_ERROR_CODES.invalidSessionToken);
318:     }
319:   }

321:   /**
322:    * Returns true when this login created the account on first use. When the account doesn't yet
323:    * exist and `allowCreate` is false (deployment signups are closed), refuses rather than creating —
324:    * existing users can still sign in.
325:    */
326:   async authenticateFromCfAccess(email: string, allowCreate: boolean): Promise<boolean> {
327:     if (!this.storage.created.get()) {
328:       if (!allowCreate) {
329:         throw new Error("New sign-ups are currently disabled on this deployment.");
330:       }
331:       // Create on first use.
332:       this.storage.created.put(true);
333:       this.storage.profile.put({
334:         type: "user",
335:         name: email.split("@")[0],
336:         id: email,
337:       });
338:       return true;
339:     }
340: 
341:     return false;
342:   }

344:   async #newSessionToken(): Promise<string> {
345:     let sessionToken = new Uint8Array(32);
346:     crypto.getRandomValues(sessionToken);
347: 
348:     let tokenId = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', sessionToken)).toHex();
349:     this.storage.sessions.put({ tokenId, created: new Date() });

351:     return sessionToken.toBase64();

354:   async login(passwordHash: Uint8Array): Promise<string | null> {
355:     let passwordHashHash = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', passwordHash));
356: 
357:     let actualHashHash = this.storage.passwordHashHash.get();
358:     if (!actualHashHash) {
359:       return null;
360:     }
361: 
362:     if (!bytesEqual(passwordHashHash, actualHashHash)) {
363:       return null;
364:     }
365: 
366:     return this.#newSessionToken();
367:   }

392:       name: displayName,
393:       id: username,
394:     });
395: 
396:     let passwordHashHash = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', passwordHash));

399:     return this.#newSessionToken();

658:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
659:   // Free-tier daily LLM-call counter (folded in from the former standalone RateLimitDO). Only used
660:   // when ENABLE_CLOUDFLARE_LIMITS is on. Single-threaded DO execution makes the read-modify-write
661:   // race-free; the window resets at UTC midnight when the stored day no longer matches.

664:   #dailyUsed(day: string): number {

669:   /** Read the current daily quota state without counting a call. */
670:   async checkDailyLlmCount(limit: number): Promise<DailyQuotaResult> {
671:     let day = utcDayKey();
672:     let used = this.#dailyUsed(day);
673:     return { withinLimits: used < limit, remaining: Math.max(0, limit - used), limit, used,
674:              resetAt: nextUtcMidnightIso() };
675:   }
676: 
677:   /**
678:    * Atomically check the daily limit and, if within it, count one call. `withinLimits` is the
679:    * pre-count decision; `used`/`remaining` reflect the state AFTER counting. No-ops once exhausted,
680:    * so a blocked request never counts.
681:    */
682:   async consumeDailyLlmCall(limit: number): Promise<DailyQuotaResult> {
683:     let day = utcDayKey();
684:     let used = this.#dailyUsed(day);
685:     if (used >= limit) {
686:       return { withinLimits: false, remaining: 0, limit, used, resetAt: nextUtcMidnightIso() };
687:     }
688:     let newUsed = used + 1;
689:     this.storage.dailyLlmCount.put({ day, count: newUsed });
690:     return { withinLimits: true, remaining: Math.max(0, limit - newUsed), limit, used: newUsed,
691:              resetAt: nextUtcMidnightIso() };
692:   }

1: // Auto-approval drain core: applies the gatekeeper's eligible pending actions (read off the sparse
2: // pendingByGatekeeper index) in id order, with a per-gatekeeper single-flight guard so two
3: // concurrent drains (the DO's input gate is open across the apply await) can't double-apply the
4: // same action. The apply is injected, keeping this constructible over a mock storage in tests.
5: 
6: import type { Collection, NonUniqueIndex } from "@gadgets/typed-storage";
7: import type { AiChatAuthorInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
8: import { createWorkshopLogger } from "./observability";
9: import type { ActionRecord, AutoApproveTagRecord } from "./overseer.js";
10: 
11: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.auto.approval");
12: 
13: export interface AutoApprovalStorage {
14:   actions: Collection<ActionRecord, number>
15:       & { pendingByGatekeeper: NonUniqueIndex<ActionRecord, number> };
16:   autoApproveTags: Collection<AutoApproveTagRecord>;
17: }
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Applies a single eligible pending action: invoke the gatekeeper, mark it approved, persist. The
21:  * caller has already validated that the record is still pending.
22:  */
23: export type ApplyPendingActionFn = (
24:     record: ActionRecord & {type: "action"},
25:     resolvedBy: AiChatAuthorInfo,
26:     autoApproved: boolean) => Promise<void>;
27: 
28: export class AutoApprovalDrainer {
29:   // Per-gatekeeper single-flight state. Key present => a drain is running for that gatekeeper; the
30:   // value is a "rerun" flag, set when another drain is requested while one is in flight, so work
31:   // submitted during a drain isn't lost.
32:   #draining = new Map<number, boolean>();
33: 
34:   constructor(
35:       private storage: AutoApprovalStorage,
36:       private applyPendingAction: ApplyPendingActionFn) {}
37: 
38:   async drain(gatekeeperId: number): Promise<void> {
39:     if (this.#draining.has(gatekeeperId)) {
40:       this.#draining.set(gatekeeperId, true);  // ask the running drain to loop again
41:       return;
42:     }
43:     this.#draining.set(gatekeeperId, false);
44:     try {
45:       do {
46:         this.#draining.set(gatekeeperId, false);
47:         await this.#drainOnce(gatekeeperId);
48:       } while (this.#draining.get(gatekeeperId));
49:     } finally {
50:       this.#draining.delete(gatekeeperId);
51:     }
52:   }
53: 
54:   // Apply all currently-eligible pending actions of the gatekeeper, in ascending id order. Stops
55:   // at the first pending action that is NOT auto-eligible (a manual gate) or that throws while
56:   // applying -- it is never skipped ahead of. This preserves in-order application and the
57:   // invariant that nothing is silently applied past a human gate.
58:   //
59:   // Eligibility requires BOTH signals: the author's `autoApprovable` verdict on the action AND a
60:   // user-enabled rule for the action's type on this gatekeeper.
61:   async #drainOnce(gatekeeperId: number): Promise<void> {
62:     // Materialize before applying: the index yields lazily in ascending id order, and applying
63:     // mutates it mid-iteration. Actions created after this snapshot trigger their own drain(),
64:     // which drain()'s rerun flag folds into this run if it's still in flight.
65:     let pending = [...this.storage.actions.pendingByGatekeeper.get(gatekeeperId)];
66: 
67:     for (let record of pending) {
68:       if (record.type !== "action") continue;
69: 
70:       let tag = record.description.actionKind?.tag;
71:       let rule = tag !== undefined
72:           ? this.storage.autoApproveTags.get(`${gatekeeperId}:${tag}`)
73:           : undefined;
74:       if (record.description.autoApprovable !== true || rule === undefined) {
75:         // A manual gate. Stop rather than skipping ahead to any later auto-eligible action.
76:         return;
77:       }
78: 
79:       // Re-check immediately before applying, to guard against a concurrent drain having already
80:       // taken this one.
81:       let fresh = this.storage.actions.get(record.id);
82:       if (!fresh || fresh.type !== "action" || fresh.state !== "pending") {
83:         continue;
84:       }
85: 
86:       try {
87:         // Attribute the auto-approval to the user who enabled the rule -- it runs under their
88:         // authority.
89:         await this.applyPendingAction(fresh, rule.enabledBy, true);
90:       } catch (err) {
91:         // Leave the action pending for manual handling and stop the drain (never skip ahead).
92:         logger.error("auto-approval failed", {
93:           event: "auto.approval.failed", actionId: fresh.id, error: err,
94:         });
95:         return;
96:       }
97:     }
98:   }

15: function normalizeText(value: string, maxLength: number): string {
16:   return value.replace(/\p{Cc}/gu, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().slice(0, maxLength);

22:  * AGENT_CATALOG_MAX_* bounds. Gatekeepers should apply the same caps before RPC, but the Workshop
23:  * does not trust them to do so. `id` keeps the full bound since it is the opaque key the agent passes
24:  * back; only the title/description need shortening. The count clamp drops from the tail so the
25:  * gatekeeper's priority order decides what survives; the survivors are then sorted for display.
26:  */
27: export function normalizeAgentCatalog(catalog: AgentCatalog): AgentCatalog {
28:   let entries = catalog.entries
29:       .map(entry => ({
30:         id: normalizeText(entry.id, AGENT_CATALOG_MAX_ID_LENGTH),
31:         title: normalizeText(entry.title, AGENT_CATALOG_MAX_TITLE_LENGTH),
32:         description: normalizeText(entry.description, AGENT_CATALOG_MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH),
33:       }))
34:       .filter(entry => entry.id.length > 0 && entry.title.length > 0);
35:   let dropped = entries.length > AGENT_CATALOG_MAX_ENTRIES;
36:   if (dropped) {
37:     logger.warn("agent catalog exceeded the entry cap", {
38:       event: "agent.catalog.truncated", size: entries.length,
39:     });
40:   }
41:   return {
42:     entries: entries
43:         .slice(0, AGENT_CATALOG_MAX_ENTRIES)
44:         .toSorted((a, b) => a.title.localeCompare(b.title) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id)),
45:     ...(catalog.truncated === true || dropped ? {truncated: true} : {}),
46:   };

50:     existing: AgentCatalogSnapshot[] | undefined,
51:     gatekeeperIds: number[],
52:     loadCatalog: (gatekeeperId: number) => Promise<AgentCatalog | null>):
53:     Promise<{snapshots: AgentCatalogSnapshot[], changed: boolean}> {
54:   let activeIds = new Set(gatekeeperIds);
55:   let existingCount = existing?.length ?? 0;
56:   let catalogs = new Map(
57:       existing
58:           ?.filter(entry => activeIds.has(entry.gatekeeperId))
59:           .map(entry => [entry.gatekeeperId, entry.catalog]));
60:   let removedStaleEntries = catalogs.size !== existingCount;
61:   let missing = gatekeeperIds.filter(gatekeeperId => !catalogs.has(gatekeeperId));

2: //
3: // This module owns all manipulation of the `collaborators` and `shareKeys` storage collections
4: // and the permission graph that links them. It deliberately performs no RPC: anything that
5: // requires talking to a User DO (resolving a profile from a username, fetching the owner's
6: // profile, notifying a user that a gadget was opened, etc.) stays in the Overseer, which passes
7: // resolved values (or, where laziness matters, a callback) into this module.
8: //
9: // LAZY REVOCATION MODEL: Access is determined by reachability from the owner in the permission
10: // graph, recomputed live at every open() (see `getEffectiveRole`). Revocation is therefore lazy:
11: // removing a collaborator only severs the edges granting *them* access, and revoking a share link
12: // only flags the link revoked. Nothing cascades, no records are deleted, and downstream edges are
13: // never touched -- users who lose their only path to the owner simply become unreachable and are
14: // denied at open() time. Because the graph is never destructively pruned, revocation is reversible:
15: // re-adding a removed collaborator restores them and, transitively, everyone they had shared with.
16: // (Records and revoked keys accumulate in storage; a future GC could reclaim long-dead entries.)

222:     fetchProfile: () => Promise<AiChatAuthorInfo>;

225:     let keyRecord = this.storage.shareKeys.get(hash);
226:     if (!keyRecord) return;

229:     // A copy of a link is an alias; follow it to the link that owns the metadata.
230:     let link = keyRecord.alias === undefined

234:     let role = link.role ?? "build";

236:     let existing = this.storage.collaborators.get(opts.profileId);
237:     if (existing) {

239:       // link (redeeming a second key of the same link is a no-op).
240:       let alreadyHasEdge = existing.addedBy.some(
241:           e => e.type === "shareKey" && e.keyId === linkId);
242:       if (!alreadyHasEdge) {
243:         existing.addedBy.push({
244:           type: "shareKey",
245:           keyId: linkId,
246:           created: new Date(),
247:           role,

249:         this.storage.collaborators.put(existing);

252:       // New collaborator -- need full profile from their user DO.
253:       let profile = await opts.fetchProfile();

256:         addedBy: [{

258:           keyId: linkId,

270:    * List currently-active collaborators -- those with a live path from the owner. Under the lazy
271:    * revocation model, removed collaborators linger in storage with no reachable role; they are
272:    * omitted here (they reappear if re-added).
273:    */

292:    * `prohibitAllSharing`). The caller may not grant a role higher than their own effective role.
293:    */

295:     caller: SharingCaller;
296:     profile: AiChatAuthorInfo;
297:     role: CollaboratorRole;
298:     note?: string;
299:   }): CollaboratorInfo {
300:     // Don't add the owner as a collaborator.
301:     if (opts.profile.id === this.ownerProfileId) {
302:       throw new Error("Cannot add the workspace owner as a collaborator.");
303:     }
304: 
305:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(opts.caller);
306:     if (roleRank(opts.role) > roleRank(callerRole)) {
307:       throw new Error("You cannot grant a role higher than your own.");
308:     }
309: 
310:     let existing = this.storage.collaborators.get(opts.profile.id);
311:     let edge: PermissionEdge = {
312:       type: "user",
313:       sharer: opts.caller.profileId,
314:       created: new Date(),
315:       role: opts.role,
316:       note: opts.note,
317:     };
318: 
319:     if (existing) {
320:       // Already a collaborator -- add an edge if they don't have one from this sharer, otherwise
321:       // upgrade the existing edge's role (never silently downgrade).
322:       let existingEdge = existing.addedBy.find(
323:           e => e.type === "user" && e.sharer === opts.caller.profileId);
324:       if (existingEdge && existingEdge.type === "user") {
325:         existingEdge.role = maxRole(edgeGrantedRole(existingEdge), opts.role);
326:         if (opts.note !== undefined) existingEdge.note = opts.note;
327:       } else {
328:         existing.addedBy.push(edge);
329:       }
330:       this.storage.collaborators.put(existing);
331:       return {
332:         profile: existing.profile,
333:         addedBy: existing.addedBy,
334:         role: this.computeEffectiveRoles().get(existing.profile.id) ?? opts.role,
335:       };
336:     }
337: 
338:     let record: CollaboratorRecord = {
339:       profile: opts.profile,
340:       addedBy: [edge],

342:     this.storage.collaborators.put(record);
343:     return {
344:       profile: record.profile,
345:       addedBy: record.addedBy,

350:   previewRemoveCollaborator(caller: SharingCaller, profileId: string): AffectedCollaborator[] {
351:     let target = this.storage.collaborators.get(profileId);

360:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, modified);

363:   /**
364:    * Remove a collaborator by severing the edges that grant them access. This is a *lazy* removal:
365:    * nothing cascades and no records are deleted. The target's record (and crucially, any edges
366:    * where the target is the *sharer* of access to others) is left intact, and dependents who lose
367:    * their only path to the owner simply become unreachable -- they are denied at open() time, not
368:    * pruned here. This makes the removal trivially reversible: re-adding the target (see
369:    * addCollaborator) restores the target and, transitively, everyone they had shared with.
370:    *
371:    *   - The owner severs *all* incoming edges to the target (owner-removal means "gone now").
372:    *   - A non-owner severs only their own `user` edge to the target; if the target retains other
373:    *     edges, they keep access (possibly at a lower role).
374:    *
375:    * `keepUsers` is optional re-root sugar: any listed dependent who would otherwise lose access or
376:    * be downgraded is granted a fresh edge from the caller at their prior role (see
377:    * `#reRootKeptUsers`). Returns the collaborators whose access actually changed (removed or
378:    * downgraded), excluding kept users.

380:   removeCollaborator(
381:       caller: SharingCaller, profileId: string, keepUsers: string[]): AffectedCollaborator[] {
382:     let target = this.storage.collaborators.get(profileId);
383:     if (!target) {
384:       throw new Error("User is not a collaborator.");

386: 
387:     // Permission check: owner can remove anyone; collaborators can only remove users
388:     // they themselves added.
389:     if (!caller.isOwner) {
390:       let hasEdgeFromCaller = target.addedBy.some(
391:           e => e.type === "user" && e.sharer === caller.profileId);
392:       if (!hasEdgeFromCaller) {
393:         throw new Error("You can only remove users that you added.");
394:       }
395:     }
396: 
397:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
398: 
399:     // Sever the edges that grant the target access. The record is retained even if it becomes
400:     // empty, so the target's own outgoing grants survive and the removal can be undone.
401:     if (caller.isOwner) {
402:       target.addedBy = [];
403:     } else {
404:       target.addedBy = target.addedBy.filter(
405:           e => !(e.type === "user" && e.sharer === caller.profileId));
406:     }
407:     this.storage.collaborators.put(target);

409:     this.#reRootKeptUsers(caller, baseline, new Set(keepUsers));

411:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, this.computeEffectiveRoles());

414:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
415:   // Share link management
416: 
417:   // Enforce that `caller` may manage `link`: the owner can manage any link; a collaborator only
418:   // the links they created. `action` is the user-facing verb (e.g. "revoke", "edit", "copy").
419:   #requireLinkManager(caller: SharingCaller, link: ShareLinkRecord, action: string): void {
420:     if (!caller.isOwner && link.createdBy !== caller.profileId) {
421:       throw new Error(`You can only ${action} share links that you created.`);
422:     }
423:   }
424: 
425:   // Look up a link by id, throwing the caller-facing error if the id is unknown or names an alias..
426:   #requireLink(linkId: string): ShareLinkRecord {
427:     let link = asLink(this.storage.shareKeys.get(linkId));
428:     if (!link) {
429:       throw new Error("Share link not found.");
430:     }
431:     return link;
432:   }
433: 
434:   async createShareLink(
435:       opts: { caller: SharingCaller; role: CollaboratorRole; note?: string })
436:       : Promise<{ key: string; linkId: string }> {
437:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(opts.caller);
438:     if (roleRank(opts.role) > roleRank(callerRole)) {
439:       throw new Error("You cannot grant a role higher than your own.");
440:     }
441: 
442:     // The link is stored as its first key: the record is keyed by that key's hash.
443:     let { key, hash } = await this.#mintKey();
444:     this.storage.shareKeys.put({
445:       id: hash,
446:       note: opts.note,
447:       created: new Date(),
448:       createdBy: opts.caller.profileId,
449:       role: opts.role,
450:     });
451:     return { key, linkId: hash };
452:   }
453: 
454:   /** Mints another key for an existing link. */
455:   async newShareLinkKey(opts: { caller: SharingCaller; linkId: string }): Promise<{ key: string }> {
456:     let link = this.#requireLink(opts.linkId);
457:     if (link.revoked) {
458:       throw new Error("Share link not found.");

460:     this.#requireLinkManager(opts.caller, link, "copy");

464:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(opts.caller);

466:       throw new Error("You cannot grant a role higher than your own.");

469:     let { key, hash } = await this.#mintKey();

473: 
474:   // Generate a random 128-bit key, returning it along with the hash it is stored under. The caller
475:   // decides whether that hash keys a link or an alias.
476:   async #mintKey(): Promise<{ key: string; hash: string }> {

480:     return { key, hash: await hashShareKey(key) };

483:   /**
484:    * Active (non-revoked) share links. The Overseer maps each `createdBy` profile.id to a display
485:    * profile (which may require RPC) to produce `ShareLinkInfo`s; see `getCreatorProfile`.
486:    */

488:     return [...this.#listLinks()].filter(link => !link.revoked);

490: 
491:   /**
492:    * Resolve the display profile for a share link's creator using only locally-available data
493:    * (the collaborator table). Returns undefined if the creator is neither a current collaborator
494:    * nor matched here (e.g. the owner), in which case the Overseer resolves it via RPC. The final
495:    * fallback (a bare profile from the id) is also the Overseer's responsibility.
496:    */
497:   getCreatorProfile(createdBy: string): AiChatAuthorInfo | undefined {
498:     return this.storage.collaborators.get(createdBy)?.profile;
499:   }
500: 
501:   updateShareLink(caller: SharingCaller, linkId: string, note?: string): void {
502:     let link = this.#requireLink(linkId);
503:     this.#requireLinkManager(caller, link, "edit");

505:     link.note = note === undefined ? undefined : note.slice(0, 500);
506:     this.storage.shareKeys.put(link);

509:   previewRevokeShareLink(caller: SharingCaller, linkId: string): AffectedCollaborator[] {
510:     let link = asLink(this.storage.shareKeys.get(linkId));
511:     if (!link) return [];
512:     this.#requireLinkManager(caller, link, "revoke");
513:     if (link.revoked) return [];

515:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
516:     let modified = this.computeEffectiveRoles({ revokedLinkId: linkId });

520:   /**
521:    * Revoke a share link by soft-revoking it (setting the `revoked` flag) rather than deleting it.
522:    * This is the lazy counterpart to removeCollaborator: the link record and every `shareKey` edge
523:    * referencing it stay intact (no dangling references), but the link contributes nothing to the
524:    * permission graph and its keys can no longer be redeemed. Its copies are deleted outright,
525:    * since no edge ever names an alias. Users who relied solely on it become unreachable and
526:    * are denied at open() time.
527:    *
528:    * `keepUsers` is optional re-root sugar, identical to removeCollaborator. Returns the
529:    * collaborators whose access actually changed (removed or downgraded), excluding kept users.
530:    */
531:   revokeShareLink(
532:       caller: SharingCaller, linkId: string, keepUsers: string[]): AffectedCollaborator[] {
533:     let link = this.#requireLink(linkId);
534:     this.#requireLinkManager(caller, link, "revoke");

536:     let baseline = this.computeEffectiveRoles();

538:     link.revoked = true;
539:     this.storage.shareKeys.put(link);

542:     this.storage.shareKeys.byAlias.delete(link.id);

544:     this.#reRootKeptUsers(caller, baseline, new Set(keepUsers));

546:     return this.#computeAffected(baseline, this.computeEffectiveRoles());

549:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
550:   // Permission-graph engine
551: 
552:   /**
553:    * Compute the effective role of every collaborator -- the maximum role reachable from the owner
554:    * through valid permission edges. A collaborator absent from the returned map has no access.
555:    *
556:    * The owner is the implicit root at "build". Each edge grants min(edge role, sharer's effective
557:    * role):
558:    *   - A "user" edge's sharer is the owner (effective "build") or another collaborator.
559:    *   - A "shareKey" edge's "sharer" is the key's creator; the edge grants the key's role bounded
560:    *     by the creator's effective role.
561:    *
562:    * Optional modifications model a hypothetical change, used by the preview methods:
563:    *   - `removedUser`: a profileId treated as removed (excluded from the graph entirely).
564:    *   - `removedEdge`: a single user edge (target ← sharer) treated as removed.
565:    *   - `revokedLinkId`: a link treated as revoked (its edges contribute nothing).
566:    */
567:   computeEffectiveRoles(opts: {
568:     removedUser?: string | null;
569:     removedEdge?: { target: string; sharer: string } | null;
570:     revokedLinkId?: string | null;
571:   } = {}): Map<string, CollaboratorRole> {
572:     let removedUser = opts.removedUser ?? null;
573:     let removedEdge = opts.removedEdge ?? null;
574:     let revokedLinkId = opts.revokedLinkId ?? null;
575: 
576:     // Map linkId → {creator, role}, excluding revoked links (the persisted `revoked` flag, and the
577:     // hypothetical `revokedLinkId` used by preview).
578:     let linkInfo = new Map<string, { creator: string; role: CollaboratorRole }>();

580:       if (link.id === revokedLinkId || link.revoked) continue;
581:       linkInfo.set(link.id, {
582:         creator: link.createdBy,
583:         role: link.role ?? "build",
584:       });
585:     }
586: 
587:     // All collaborators except the removed user.
588:     let allCollabs = new Map<string, CollaboratorRecord>();
589:     for (let record of this.storage.collaborators.list()) {
590:       if (record.profile.id !== removedUser) {
591:         allCollabs.set(record.profile.id, record);
592:       }
593:     }
594: 
595:     // Roles known so far.
596:     let eff = new Map<string, CollaboratorRole>();
597: 
598:     // Effective role of a potential sharer (the owner is the root at "build").
599:     let sharerRole = (id: string): CollaboratorRole | undefined =>
600:         id === this.ownerProfileId ? "build" : eff.get(id);
601: 
602:     // Fixed-point iteration. Roles only increase, so this converges.
603:     let changed = true;
604:     while (changed) {
605:       changed = false;
606:       for (let [id, record] of allCollabs) {
607:         let best: CollaboratorRole | undefined = eff.get(id);
608:         for (let edge of record.addedBy) {
609:           let granted: CollaboratorRole | undefined;
610:           if (edge.type === "shareKey") {
611:             let info = linkInfo.get(edge.keyId);
612:             if (!info) continue;  // link revoked or no longer exists
613:             let creatorRole = sharerRole(info.creator);
614:             if (!creatorRole) continue;
615:             granted = minRole(info.role, creatorRole);
616:           } else {
617:             // Skip the specifically-removed edge.
618:             if (removedEdge && id === removedEdge.target &&
619:                 edge.sharer === removedEdge.sharer) {
620:               continue;
621:             }
622:             if (edge.sharer === removedUser) continue;
623:             let upstream = sharerRole(edge.sharer);
624:             if (!upstream) continue;
625:             granted = minRole(edgeGrantedRole(edge), upstream);
626:           }
627:           if (granted && (!best || roleRank(granted) > roleRank(best))) {
628:             best = granted;
629:           }
630:         }
631:         if (best && best !== eff.get(id)) {
632:           eff.set(id, best);
633:           changed = true;
634:         }
635:       }
636:     }

638:     return eff;
639:   }

641:   // The caller's effective role, throwing if the caller has no access at all (which should not
642:   // happen for an authorized session).
643:   #requireCallerRole(caller: SharingCaller): CollaboratorRole {
644:     if (caller.isOwner) return "build";
645:     let role = this.computeEffectiveRoles().get(caller.profileId);
646:     if (!role) {
647:       throw new Error("You do not have permission to share this workspace.");
648:     }
649:     return role;
650:   }
651: 
652:   // Diff two effective-role maps, returning the collaborators whose access changed. A user is
653:   // affected if they had access in `baseline` and either lost it (newRole null) or were downgraded
654:   // (newRole lower than oldRole) in `modified`. Profiles/edges are read from current storage.
655:   #computeAffected(
656:       baseline: Map<string, CollaboratorRole>,
657:       modified: Map<string, CollaboratorRole>): AffectedCollaborator[] {
658:     let result: AffectedCollaborator[] = [];
659:     for (let [id, oldRole] of baseline) {
660:       let newRole = modified.get(id) ?? null;
661:       if (newRole !== null && roleRank(newRole) >= roleRank(oldRole)) {
662:         continue;  // unchanged or (shouldn't happen) upgraded
663:       }
664:       let record = this.storage.collaborators.get(id);
665:       if (!record) continue;
666:       result.push({
667:         profile: record.profile,
668:         addedBy: record.addedBy,
669:         oldRole,
670:         newRole,
671:       });
672:     }
673:     return result;
674:   }
675: 
676:   // Optional re-root sugar for removeCollaborator/revokeShareLink. Must be called *after* the
677:   // edge/key has already been severed in storage. `baseline` is the effective-role map from before
678:   // the severance. For each kept user who would otherwise lose access or be downgraded, append a
679:   // fresh `user` edge from the caller at their prior role (bounded by what the caller can grant),
680:   // so they retain their access independently of the severed path.
681:   #reRootKeptUsers(
682:       caller: SharingCaller, baseline: Map<string, CollaboratorRole>, keepSet: Set<string>): void {
683:     if (keepSet.size === 0) return;
684: 
685:     let callerRole = this.#requireCallerRole(caller);
686:     let afterSever = this.computeEffectiveRoles();
687: 
688:     for (let id of keepSet) {
689:       let prior = baseline.get(id);
690:       if (!prior) continue;  // had no access to begin with -- nothing to keep
691: 
692:       let now = afterSever.get(id);
693:       if (now && roleRank(now) >= roleRank(prior)) continue;  // not dropped -- no edge needed
694: 
695:       let record = this.storage.collaborators.get(id);
696:       if (!record) continue;
697: 
698:       record.addedBy.push({
699:         type: "user",
700:         sharer: caller.profileId,
701:         created: new Date(),
702:         role: minRole(prior, callerRole),
703:       });
704:       this.storage.collaborators.put(record);
705:     }
706:   }

2: //
3: // Each workspace's Overseer DO holds a real git object database -- SHA-1, zlib-deflated loose
4: // objects, byte-identical to what `git` itself would write -- stored in the `gitObjects`
5: // typed-storage collection. Mainline gadget code is (will be, once the commit-backed code flow
6: // lands) represented as commits in this store, with each GadgetRecord pointing at its head
7: // commit.
8: //
9: // There is deliberately no ref layer: no branches, tags, or HEAD. Our "refs" are the gadget
10: // records, blueprint records, and chats' pinned commits, all managed by the Overseer's own
11: // workflow. Because the store is content-addressed and refless, unrelated histories coexist
12: // freely in the same collection, and related histories (gadgets forked from each other or
13: // instantiated from the same blueprint) deduplicate at the blob/tree level.
14: //
15: // We use real git formats (rather than a git-shaped custom encoding) so that gadget code can
16: // later be exported to and imported from real git repositories, and so agents can eventually
17: // "mount" arbitrary repos through gatekeeper-gated push/pull. isomorphic-git provides the object
18: // codec; we use only its plumbing (writeBlob/writeTree/writeCommit/read*/log), which operates
19: // against a gitdir containing nothing but `objects/**`. The porcelain is off-limits:
20: // `git.commit` requires HEAD/index/config, and `git.merge` cannot represent the merge behavior
21: // we want (see `threeWayMerge`).
22: //
23: // Storage notes:
24: // - Loose objects only, one collection record per object, keyed by oid. isomorphic-git never
25: //   writes deltified data (it only reads deltas in packfiles fetched from remotes), so each
26: //   record is a zlib'd whole object. Dedup comes from content addressing, not deltas.
27: // - No object exceeds ~2MB today (records hold single source files, small trees, and commit
28: //   headers). If large blobs ever appear, chunking records or spilling to R2 is a change local
29: //   to the fs shim below.
30: // - No GC. Dangling objects are only created by accepted merges, imports, and migration -- never
31: //   by in-flight chats -- and are cheap. If GC is ever needed, the roots are enumerable: gadget
32: //   records, blueprint gadget records, live chats' pinned commits, the pin declarations in chat
33: //   logs and compaction checkpoints (closed epochs are reconstructed from them), and the
34: //   `observedCommit` stamps on chats' readFile tool calls (which nothing else roots -- a future
35: //   GC must either root them or the agent's elision path must tolerate a missing commit by
36: //   eliding unconditionally).
37: 
38: import {
39:   readBlob,
40:   readCommit,
41:   readTree,
42:   writeBlob,
43:   writeCommit,
44:   writeTree,
45:   log,
46:   type PromiseFsClient,
47:   type TreeEntry,
48: } from "isomorphic-git";
49: import diff3Merge from "diff3";
50: import { collection, type Collection } from "@gadgets/typed-storage";
51: import type { AiChatAuthorInfo, CommitIdentity, CommitInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
52: 
53: // =======================================================================================
54: // Storage schema
55: 
56: /**
57:  * One git loose object: `data` is the zlib-deflated object exactly as git would store it under
58:  * `.git/objects/xx/yyyy...`, and `oid` is its 40-hex SHA-1 name. Content-addressed, hence
59:  * immutable and idempotent to rewrite.
60:  */
61: export interface GitObjectRecord {
62:   oid: string;
63:   data: Uint8Array;
64: }
65: 
66: /**
67:  * Typed-storage schema for a git object store collection. Shared between `makeOverseerStorage()`
68:  * and tests so both bind the identical schema.
69:  */
70: export function gitObjectsCollection() {
71:   return collection<GitObjectRecord>()({
72:     primaryKey: "oid",
73:   });
74: }
75: 
76: // =======================================================================================
77: // fs shim
78: //
79: // isomorphic-git's only storage interface is a filesystem. We give it a virtual one that maps
80: // loose-object paths onto the `gitObjects` collection and rejects everything else, so we never
81: // silently accept writes we didn't intend to store. If we ever need non-object paths (e.g. for
82: // git protocol support), that's a schema extension we design then.
83: 
84: /** The virtual gitdir path the fs shim serves. Only meaningful within this module and tests. */
85: export const GITDIR = "/git";
86: 
87: const LOOSE_OBJECT_PATH = new RegExp(`^${GITDIR}/objects/([0-9a-f]{2})/([0-9a-f]{38})$`);
88: 
89: /** Parses a loose-object path within the virtual gitdir into its 40-hex oid. */
90: function oidFromLoosePath(path: unknown): string | undefined {
91:   if (typeof path !== "string") return undefined;
92:   let match = LOOSE_OBJECT_PATH.exec(path);
93:   if (!match) return undefined;
94:   return match[1] + match[2];
95: }
96: 
97: /** Makes an Error carrying the `code` property Node-style fs consumers dispatch on. */
98: function fsError(code: string, message: string): Error {
99:   return Object.assign(new Error(`${code}: ${message}`), { code });
100: }
101: 
102: /**
103:  * A `PromiseFsClient` backed by a `gitObjects` collection. Exposed for tests; production code
104:  * should use `GitStore`.
105:  *
106:  * Contract subtleties, verified against isomorphic-git 1.40:
107:  * - All ten methods must exist even though only `readFile`/`writeFile`/`stat`/`mkdir`/`readdir`
108:  *   are ever exercised for object-database work: `bindFs` binds every one unconditionally.
109:  * - The promise-style detection probe calls `readFile()` with no arguments and requires a
110:  *   promise back; `async` methods satisfy this by returning a rejected promise rather than
111:  *   throwing synchronously.
112:  * - Missing files must reject with `code: "ENOENT"`: `FileSystem.exists()` rethrows anything
113:  *   else, and `discoverGitdir` / `FileSystem.read` / `FileSystem.readdir` tolerate rejections
114:  *   (the gitdir itself, `shallow`, and `objects/pack` reads all take those paths).
115:  */
116: export function makeGitObjectsFs(objects: Collection<GitObjectRecord, string>): PromiseFsClient {
117:   return { promises: {
118:     async readFile(path: unknown): Promise<Uint8Array> {
119:       let oid = oidFromLoosePath(path);
120:       if (oid === undefined) throw fsError("ENOENT", `unsupported read: ${String(path)}`);
121:       let record = objects.get(oid);
122:       if (record === undefined) throw fsError("ENOENT", `no such object: ${oid}`);
123:       return record.data;
124:     },
125: 
126:     async writeFile(path: unknown, data: unknown): Promise<void> {
127:       let oid = oidFromLoosePath(path);
128:       if (oid === undefined) throw fsError("EPERM", `unsupported write: ${String(path)}`);
129:       if (!(data instanceof Uint8Array)) throw fsError("EINVAL", "expected binary object data");
130:       // Copy: the input is typically a Buffer view over a shared pool, and the record outlives
131:       // the call.
132:       objects.put({ oid, data: new Uint8Array(data) });
133:     },
134: 
135:     async stat(path: unknown): Promise<{
136:       isFile(): boolean;
137:       isDirectory(): boolean;
138:       isSymbolicLink(): boolean;
139:       size: number;
140:     }> {
141:       // Only existing loose objects stat successfully. The gitdir itself rejecting is fine:
142:       // discoverGitdir treats a failed stat as "neither file nor directory" and uses the path
143:       // as-is.
144:       let oid = oidFromLoosePath(path);
145:       let record = oid === undefined ? undefined : objects.get(oid);
146:       if (record === undefined) throw fsError("ENOENT", `no such file: ${String(path)}`);
147:       let size = record.data.byteLength;
148:       return {
149:         isFile: () => true,
150:         isDirectory: () => false,
151:         isSymbolicLink: () => false,
152:         size,
153:       };
154:     },
155: 
156:     async mkdir(_path: unknown): Promise<void> {
157:       // Directories don't exist in this store; object writes succeed without them. Accept and
158:       // ignore so `FileSystem.write`'s mkdirp fallback can't fail.
159:     },
160: 
161:     async readdir(path: unknown): Promise<string[]> {
162:       // The packed-object probe lists `objects/pack`; we store no packfiles, so it's empty.
163:       if (path === `${GITDIR}/objects/pack`) return [];
164:       throw fsError("ENOENT", `unsupported readdir: ${String(path)}`);
165:     },
166: 
167:     // Never used for object-database work, but bindFs requires them to exist.
168:     async lstat(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
169:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `lstat unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
170:     },
171:     async unlink(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
172:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `unlink unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
173:     },
174:     async rmdir(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
175:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `rmdir unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
176:     },
177:     async readlink(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
178:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `readlink unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
179:     },
180:     async symlink(path: unknown): Promise<never> {
181:       throw fsError("ENOSYS", `symlink unsupported by git-store: ${String(path)}`);
182:     },
183:   } };
184: }

186: // =======================================================================================
187: // GitStore
188: 
189: /** Options for `GitStore.writeFilesAsCommit()`. */
190: export interface WriteCommitOptions {
191:   /** Parent commit oids; empty for a root commit. */
192:   parents: string[];
193: 
194:   /** Commit author. Also used as the committer unless `committer` is given. */
195:   author: CommitIdentity;
196: 
197:   /** Committer, when distinct from the author. */
198:   committer?: CommitIdentity;
199: 
200:   /** Commit message. Normalized git-style to end with exactly one newline. */
201:   message: string;
202: 
203:   /** Author and committer timestamp. Recorded in UTC (timezone offset 0). */
204:   timestamp: Date;
205: }
206: 
207: // A parsed-but-unwritten tree: file contents at the leaves, subtrees within.
208: type TreeNode = Map<string, TreeNode | string>;
209: 
210: /**
211:  * A git object database over a `gitObjects` collection.
212:  *
213:  * This is plumbing only: it reads and writes blobs/trees/commits by oid and knows nothing about
214:  * refs -- callers (gadget records, blueprint records, chat pins) track which commits matter.
215:  * Files are presented as flat `path -> text` maps; paths may contain `/`, which maps to nested
216:  * trees so stored history stays interoperable with real git tooling.
217:  *
218:  * Construct one per Overseer instance and reuse it: it carries isomorphic-git's parse cache.
219:  */
220: export class GitStore {
221:   #fs: PromiseFsClient;
222:   #cache: object = {};
223: 
224:   constructor(objects: Collection<GitObjectRecord, string>) {
225:     this.#fs = makeGitObjectsFs(objects);
226:   }
227: 
228:   /**
229:    * Writes `files` (a `path -> text` map) as a commit, returning the commit oid. All objects are
230:    * content-addressed, so rewriting identical content is a cheap no-op that produces the same
231:    * oids.
232:    */
233:   async writeFilesAsCommit(
234:       files: ReadonlyMap<string, string>, options: WriteCommitOptions): Promise<string> {
235:     let tree = await this.#writeTreeNode(buildTreeNode(files));
236:     let when = { timestamp: Math.floor(options.timestamp.getTime() / 1000), timezoneOffset: 0 };
237:     return await writeCommit({
238:       fs: this.#fs,
239:       gitdir: GITDIR,
240:       commit: {
241:         message: options.message,
242:         tree,
243:         parent: [...options.parents],
244:         author: { ...options.author, ...when },
245:         committer: { ...(options.committer ?? options.author), ...when },
246:       },
247:     });
248:   }
249: 
250:   /**
251:    * Reads back the full file map of a commit: the inverse of `writeFilesAsCommit()`, with nested
252:    * trees flattened to `/`-joined paths.
253:    *
254:    * Only regular-file blobs (modes 100644/100755) are supported; symlinks and submodules --
255:    * which we never write, but an imported history could contain -- are rejected rather than
256:    * misread.
257:    */
258:   async readCommitFiles(oid: string): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
259:     let { commit } = await readCommit({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache });
260:     let files = new Map<string, string>();
261:     await this.#collectTreeFiles(commit.tree, "", files);
262:     return files;
263:   }
264: 
265:   /**
266:    * Reads a commit's tree as a `path -> blob oid` map (flattened like `readCommitFiles`, but
267:    * without touching blob content). Content addressing makes this the cheap way to ask which
268:    * files differ between two commits -- see `changedPaths`.
269:    */
270:   async commitFileOids(oid: string): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
271:     let { commit } = await readCommit({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache });
272:     let out = new Map<string, string>();
273:     await this.#collectTreeOids(commit.tree, "", out);
274:     return out;
275:   }
276: 
277:   /**
278:    * The set of file paths whose content differs between two commits' trees (added, removed, or
279:    * changed), compared by oid -- equal subtrees short-circuit without descending, and no blob
280:    * content is ever read. `undefined` on either side means an empty tree, so a one-sided call
281:    * lists a commit's whole tree.
282:    */
283:   async changedPaths(a: string | undefined, b: string | undefined): Promise<Set<string>> {
284:     let changed = new Set<string>();
285:     if (a === b) return changed;
286:     let treeOf = async (oid: string | undefined) => oid === undefined ? undefined
287:         : (await readCommit({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache }))
288:             .commit.tree;
289:     await this.#diffTrees(await treeOf(a), await treeOf(b), "", changed);
290:     return changed;
291:   }
292: 
293:   // Accumulates the paths that differ between two trees (either may be absent = empty) into
294:   // `out`. Entries are matched by name; a name that is a blob on one side and a tree on the
295:   // other contributes every path under both sides.
296:   async #diffTrees(aOid: string | undefined, bOid: string | undefined, prefix: string,
297:                    out: Set<string>): Promise<void> {
298:     if (aOid === bOid) return;
299:     let entriesOf = async (oid: string | undefined) => {
300:       if (oid === undefined) return new Map<string, TreeEntry>();
301:       let { tree } = await readTree({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid, cache: this.#cache });
302:       return new Map(tree.map(entry => [entry.path, entry]));
303:     };
304:     let aEntries = await entriesOf(aOid);
305:     let bEntries = await entriesOf(bOid);
306:     for (let name of new Set([...aEntries.keys(), ...bEntries.keys()])) {
307:       let a = aEntries.get(name);
308:       let b = bEntries.get(name);
309:       if (a?.oid === b?.oid && a?.type === b?.type) continue;
310:       let path = prefix + name;
311:       if (a?.type === "tree" || b?.type === "tree") {
312:         // Descend the tree side(s); a blob opposite a tree is one more difference at `path`.
313:         await this.#diffTrees(a?.type === "tree" ? a.oid : undefined,
314:                               b?.type === "tree" ? b.oid : undefined, `${path}/`, out);
315:         if (a?.type === "blob" || b?.type === "blob") out.add(path);
316:       } else {
317:         out.add(path);
318:       }
319:     }
320:   }
321: 
322:   /**
323:    * Walks the commit graph from `oid` (the commit itself first, then its ancestry), returning up
324:    * to `depth` commits' metadata. Traversal order for merge commits follows git log's default
325:    * (reverse chronological).
326:    */
327:   async readCommitLog(oid: string, options: { depth?: number } = {}): Promise<CommitInfo[]> {
328:     let entries = await log({
329:       fs: this.#fs,
330:       gitdir: GITDIR,
331:       ref: oid,
332:       depth: options.depth,
333:       cache: this.#cache,
334:     });
335:     return entries.map(entry => ({
336:       oid: entry.oid,
337:       parents: entry.commit.parent,
338:       message: entry.commit.message,
339:       author: { name: entry.commit.author.name, email: entry.commit.author.email },
340:       timestamp: new Date(entry.commit.author.timestamp * 1000),
341:     }));
342:   }
343: 
344:   async #writeTreeNode(node: TreeNode): Promise<string> {
345:     let entries: TreeEntry[] = [];
346:     for (let [name, child] of node) {
347:       if (typeof child === "string") {
348:         let oid = await writeBlob({
349:           fs: this.#fs,
350:           gitdir: GITDIR,
351:           blob: new TextEncoder().encode(child),
352:         });
353:         entries.push({ mode: "100644", path: name, oid, type: "blob" });
354:       } else {
355:         let oid = await this.#writeTreeNode(child);
356:         entries.push({ mode: "040000", path: name, oid, type: "tree" });
357:       }
358:     }
359:     // isomorphic-git sorts entries into git's canonical tree order itself.
360:     return await writeTree({ fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, tree: entries });
361:   }
362: 
363:   // The oid-level analog of #collectTreeFiles: flattens a tree to `path -> blob oid` without
364:   // reading any blob. Applies the same mode restriction, so the two views can never disagree
365:   // about which paths exist.
366:   async #collectTreeOids(
367:       treeOid: string, prefix: string, out: Map<string, string>): Promise<void> {
368:     let { tree } = await readTree(
369:         { fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid: treeOid, cache: this.#cache });
370:     for (let entry of tree) {
371:       let path = prefix + entry.path;
372:       if (entry.type === "tree") {
373:         await this.#collectTreeOids(entry.oid, `${path}/`, out);
374:       } else if (entry.type === "blob" && (entry.mode === "100644" || entry.mode === "100755")) {
375:         out.set(path, entry.oid);
376:       } else {
377:         throw new Error(`unsupported tree entry at ${path}: mode ${entry.mode}`);
378:       }
379:     }
380:   }
381: 
382:   async #collectTreeFiles(
383:       treeOid: string, prefix: string, out: Map<string, string>): Promise<void> {
384:     let { tree } = await readTree(
385:         { fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid: treeOid, cache: this.#cache });
386:     for (let entry of tree) {
387:       let path = prefix + entry.path;
388:       if (entry.type === "tree") {
389:         await this.#collectTreeFiles(entry.oid, `${path}/`, out);
390:       } else if (entry.type === "blob" && (entry.mode === "100644" || entry.mode === "100755")) {
391:         let { blob } = await readBlob(
392:             { fs: this.#fs, gitdir: GITDIR, oid: entry.oid, cache: this.#cache });
393:         out.set(path, new TextDecoder().decode(blob));
394:       } else {
395:         throw new Error(`unsupported tree entry at ${path}: mode ${entry.mode}`);
396:       }
397:     }
398:   }
399: }
400: 
401: // Converts a flat `path -> text` map into nested tree nodes, validating path shape as we go:
402: // git can't represent empty segments or "."/"..", and a path can't be both a file and a
403: // directory.
404: function buildTreeNode(files: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): TreeNode {
405:   let root: TreeNode = new Map();
406:   for (let [path, content] of files) {
407:     let segments = path.split("/");
408:     let node = root;
409:     for (let [i, segment] of segments.entries()) {
410:       if (segment === "" || segment === "." || segment === "..") {
411:         throw new Error(`invalid file path: ${path}`);
412:       }
413:       let last = i === segments.length - 1;
414:       let existing = node.get(segment);
415:       if (last) {
416:         if (existing !== undefined) throw new Error(`conflicting file paths at: ${path}`);
417:         node.set(segment, content);
418:       } else {
419:         if (existing === undefined) {
420:           existing = new Map();
421:           node.set(segment, existing);
422:         } else if (typeof existing === "string") {
423:           throw new Error(`conflicting file paths at: ${path}`);
424:         }
425:         node = existing;
426:       }
427:     }
428:   }
429:   return root;
430: }
431: 
432: /** Compares two flattened file maps for identical content. */
433: export function filesEqual(
434:     a: ReadonlyMap<string, string>, b: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): boolean {
435:   if (a.size !== b.size) return false;
436:   for (let [name, content] of a) {
437:     if (b.get(name) !== content) return false;
438:   }
439:   return true;
440: }

442: // =======================================================================================
443: // Three-way merge
444: 
445: /** Labels for the three sides of a merge, rendered into conflict markers. */
446: export interface MergeLabels {
447:   base?: string;
448:   ours?: string;
449:   theirs?: string;
450: }
451: 
452: /** The result of `threeWayMerge()`. */
453: export interface MergeResult {
454:   /** The merged file map, including any files containing conflict markers. */
455:   files: Map<string, string>;
456: 
457:   /**
458:    * Paths whose merge was not clean, in sorted order. Content conflicts carry inline 3-way
459:    * markers; delete-vs-modify conflicts keep the modified content with no markers.
460:    */
461:   conflictPaths: string[];
462: }
463: 
464: /**
465:  * Merges three file maps: `base` is the common ancestor, `ours` and `theirs` the two sides.
466:  * Never throws on conflict -- conflicted files get inline 3-way markers
467:  * (`<<<<<<<`/`|||||||`/`=======`/`>>>>>>>`, diff3 style) and are reported in `conflictPaths`,
468:  * for the user or their agent to clean up.
469:  *
470:  * This deliberately replaces both Yjs merging (CRDT merge across divergent bases produces
471:  * nonsense) and isomorphic-git's `merge`/`mergeTree` (which throw on both-sides-added conflicts
472:  * before any merge driver runs, and require an index). The common ancestor is always explicitly
473:  * known in our workflow -- the chat's last merged commit -- so no merge-base discovery is
474:  * needed.
475:  *
476:  * Per-file semantics:
477:  * - changed on one side only (including deletion): that side wins;
478:  * - identical change on both sides (including both deleted): clean;
479:  * - deleted on one side, changed on the other: the changed content survives, reported as a
480:  *   conflict;
481:  * - changed on both sides (including both-added): line merged via diff3, conflicting hunks
482:  *   marked.
483:  */
484: export function threeWayMerge(
485:     base: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
486:     ours: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
487:     theirs: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
488:     labels: MergeLabels = {}): MergeResult {
489:   let files = new Map<string, string>();
490:   let conflictPaths: string[] = [];
491: 
492:   let allPaths = [...new Set([...base.keys(), ...ours.keys(), ...theirs.keys()])].toSorted();
493:   for (let path of allPaths) {
494:     let b = base.get(path);
495:     let o = ours.get(path);
496:     let t = theirs.get(path);
497: 
498:     if (o === t) {
499:       // Identical on both sides (possibly both deleted, possibly an identical add).
500:       if (o !== undefined) files.set(path, o);
501:     } else if (o === b) {
502:       // Only theirs changed (possibly a deletion).
503:       if (t !== undefined) files.set(path, t);
504:     } else if (t === b) {
505:       // Only ours changed (possibly a deletion).
506:       if (o !== undefined) files.set(path, o);
507:     } else if (o === undefined || t === undefined) {
508:       // Deleted on one side, changed on the other: keep the modified content.
509:       files.set(path, (o ?? t)!);
510:       conflictPaths.push(path);
511:     } else {
512:       // Changed on both sides (b === undefined means both-added with different content; diff3
513:       // against an empty base marks the entirety of both sides as conflicting).
514:       let merged = mergeText(b ?? "", o, t, labels);
515:       files.set(path, merged.text);
516:       if (!merged.clean) conflictPaths.push(path);
517:     }
518:   }
519: 
520:   return { files, conflictPaths };
521: }
522: 
523: // A zero-width boundary after every "\n"; split() then keeps each terminator with its line.
524: const LINE_BOUNDARY = /(?<=\n)/;
525: 
526: /**
527:  * Split `text` into lines, each keeping its trailing "\n", so `lines.join("") === text` always
528:  * holds. The consumer -- the diff3 merge below -- reassembles content from the pieces it
529:  * computes over, so the split must be
530:  * lossless above all: only "\n" ends a line, and a bare "\r" (or U+2028/U+2029) stays *inside*
531:  * its line rather than acting as a boundary, which merely makes diffs and merges of such exotic

564:       text += `||||||| ${labels.base ?? "base"}\n`;
565:       text += withFinalNewline(region.conflict.o.join(""));
566:       text += "=======\n";
567:       text += withFinalNewline(region.conflict.b.join(""));
568:       text += `>>>>>>> ${labels.theirs ?? "theirs"}\n`;
569:     }

1: // Installing the deployment's bundled output-format blueprints.
2: //
3: // The archives and their presentation come from a directory chosen at build time (see
4: // scripts/build-format-blueprints.mjs), so a deployment ships its own formats by pointing
5: // FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR at its own tree rather than by editing this repo.
6: //
7: // Installation writes an ordinary blueprint -- metadata into BLUEPRINTS, the code snapshot into
8: // BLUEPRINT_CONTENT -- exactly as publishing does. Nothing downstream knows these are special:
9: // no reserved id prefix, no fallback branch in the read path. Failure is tolerable: a deployment
10: // with none installed simply has no standard formats.
11: 
12: import { BlueprintMetadata, BlueprintPublicInfo } from "@gadgets/workshop-shared/api";
13: import { BlueprintKvRecord, parseBlueprintArchive } from "./blueprint-archive.js";
14: import { BundledFormatBlueprint, FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS } from "./generated/format-blueprints.js";
15: import { fingerprint } from "./admin-config.js";
16: import { createWorkshopLogger } from "./observability";
17: 
18: const logger = createWorkshopLogger("workshop.formats");
19: 
20: type InstallEnv = Pick<Cloudflare.Env, "BLUEPRINTS" | "BLUEPRINT_CONTENT">;
21: 
22: /**
23:  * Identifies the exact set of bundled blueprints a deployment has installed, and how. Compared
24:  * with what was installed last time, so any change here triggers reinstallation.
25:  *
26:  * Everything that ends up in the installed metadata contributes, not just `revision`: editing a
27:  * description would otherwise build, deploy, and change nothing on a deployment that had already
28:  * installed. `revision` covers the one input this can't see, the archive bytes.
29:  */
30: export function formatBlueprintsManifestVersion(): string {
31:   return FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS
32:       .map(e => `${e.blueprintId}@${e.revision}+` +
33:           fingerprint(JSON.stringify([e.title, e.description, e.author, e.output])))
34:       .toSorted()
35:       .join(",");
36: }
37: 
38: // Install one bundled blueprint, returning its public info for the featured mirror.
39: async function installOne(env: InstallEnv, entry: BundledFormatBlueprint)
40:     : Promise<BlueprintPublicInfo> {
41:   // Parse through the ordinary archive reader so a corrupt bundled file fails the same way an
42:   // uploaded one would, rather than producing a half-installed blueprint.
43:   let {metadata, contentLength, content} = await parseBlueprintArchive(
44:       new Response(Uint8Array.fromBase64(entry.archive) as BufferSource).body!);
45: 
46:   // R2 needs a known length, and the archive is already fully in memory (it came out of the
47:   // Worker bundle), so buffer rather than plumbing a FixedLengthStream through as the upload path
48:   // does for genuinely streamed uploads.
49:   let contentBytes = new Uint8Array(await new Response(content).arrayBuffer());
50:   if (contentBytes.byteLength !== contentLength) {
51:     throw new Error(`Archive declares ${contentLength} content bytes but holds ` +
52:         `${contentBytes.byteLength}.`);
53:   }
54: 
55:   // The archive supplies what the blueprint does -- code, bindings, and the dates from the
56:   // workspace it was exported from. How it is presented comes from its sidecar, overwriting
57:   // whatever the archive carries.
58:   let installed: BlueprintMetadata = {
59:     ...metadata,
60:     title: entry.title,
61:     description: entry.description,
62:     author: entry.author,
63:     output: entry.output,
64:   };
65: 
66:   // Content first: a blueprint whose metadata exists but whose R2 object doesn't is broken, while
67:   // the reverse is merely an orphaned object that the next install overwrites. The archive's
68:   // content section is already gzip-compressed, which is exactly what R2 holds.
69:   await env.BLUEPRINT_CONTENT.put(`${entry.blueprintId}/${installed.version}`, contentBytes);
70: 
71:   let kvRecord: BlueprintKvRecord = {metadata: installed};
72:   await env.BLUEPRINTS.put(entry.blueprintId, JSON.stringify(kvRecord));
73: 
74:   return {id: entry.blueprintId, metadata: installed};
75: }
76: 
77: /**
78:  * Install every bundled blueprint, skipping (and logging) any that fail. Returns the public info
79:  * of those that installed, so the caller can offer them to users.
80:  */
81: export async function installFormatBlueprints(env: InstallEnv): Promise<BlueprintPublicInfo[]> {
82:   let installed: BlueprintPublicInfo[] = [];
83:   for (let entry of FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS) {
84:     try {
85:       installed.push(await installOne(env, entry));
86:       logger.info("installed format blueprint", {
87:         event: "formats.install.ok", blueprintId: entry.blueprintId,
88:       });
89:     } catch (err) {
90:       // One bad archive must not deny the deployment the others.
91:       logger.error("failed to install format blueprint", {
92:         event: "formats.install.failed", blueprintId: entry.blueprintId, error: err,
93:       });
94:     }
95:   }
96:   return installed;
97: }

6: // submodule, so a fork can't add files here without conflicting on every update -- it keeps its
7: // archives in its own tree and points the build at them. Whatever directory is named *is* the
8: // deployment's format set; it replaces this one rather than adding to it.
9: //
10: // Each blueprint is a `<name>.gadget` archive and a `<name>.json` beside it describing how to
11: // present it. Nothing references a list, so a directory outside this repo is self-contained.
12: //
13: // Archives are binary, so they are emitted as base64 -- the same "bundle a data file as a
14: // generated module" approach gatekeeper-context uses for its SPA.

24:

26: // runs before (and without) a TypeScript build; the runtime validates against the real list, so
27: // the cost of drift is a build that rejects an icon the Worker would have accepted.
28: const OUTPUT_ICONS = ["fileText", "gridNine", "presentation", "appWindow", "flowArrow",
29:     "kanban", "chartBar", "table", "notebook", "listChecks"];
30: 
31: // Must match isReservedBlueprintKey() in src/blueprint-archive.ts. This build script runs without
32: // loading TypeScript modules, so keep the tiny control-key list here as well.
33: const RESERVED_BLUEPRINT_KEYS = new Set([".featured", ".adminConfig"]);
34: 
35: // Validated here rather than at runtime so a typo fails the build of whoever made it, instead of
36: // quietly presenting the wrong thing in production. Unknown keys are rejected too: silently
37: // ignoring one looks exactly like the field not working.
38: function parseSidecar(name, raw) {
39:   let bad = (message) => { throw new Error(`${name}.json: ${message}`); };
40:   let parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
41: 
42:   let string = (value, what) => {

48:   if (Object.keys(rest).length > 0) bad(`unknown keys: ${Object.keys(rest).join(", ")}`);
